releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

**Kernel extensions.** A new `kernel.sh` covers the areas this module had not touched: devfreq bus and memory-controller clocks, KSM deduplication, transparent hugepages, `schedtune` boost, the full three-value TCP buffers, touch boost, and the filesystem ceilings (inotify, file-max, nr_open). Each section has its own switch and all of them are off by default.

**Config versioning.** Config writes now go through a temp file and an atomic rename rather than `sed -i`, so an interrupted write can no longer leave a half-written file. There is a `SCHEMA` field and a migration path that fills in new keys on existing installs without disturbing what is already set.

**SELinux.** The module now ships `sepolicy.rule` with 184 rules covering the nodes it writes. Previously some writes could be silently blocked on enforcing devices.

**Watchdog.** `watchdog.sh` checks autopilot, guard, appwatch and wipeshield every five minutes and restarts anything that died. They used to fail silently.

**Also**
- periodic TRIM, interval in days
- switch to powersave automatically below a battery level you choose
- dry run now reports what the kernel extensions would change
- WebUI: kernel extension switches, watchdog controls, devfreq listing

**Fixed**
- safe mode appended `SAFEGUARD=0` to the config, creating a duplicate key. It rewrites in place now
- the boot-failure counter was left as an empty file when cleared

Everything from earlier versions is unchanged.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

**License** - the repo now carries the GPL-3.0 text that module.yaml was already claiming.

**Custom presets** - save your own named profile on top of one of the four built-ins. Names are validated, and you cannot shadow a built-in.

**Per-app parameters** - a node and value can be bound to a package and written only while that package is in the foreground. Range checking applies. Useful for capping one game's clocks without slowing everything else.

**Dry-run preview** - before applying anything, ask what would change. It prints every node with its current and target value and writes nothing at all.

**Also in this build**
- CHANGELOG.md covering every release so far
- English readme, linked from the Chinese one
- a tools tab in the WebUI for backup, presets, per-app parameters and the preview, 9 tabs total

**Fixed**
- app-revert silently restored nothing: it looked up backups by the unprefixed path while the writer stored them with the KSU_SYS prefix
- the per-app code was initially inserted inside another function and broke the script; custom.sh was rewritten with all functions at top level

Everything from earlier versions is unchanged: four profiles, adaptive switching, charge limiting, app standby management, custom parameters, display tuning, boot-failure rollback, wipe protection and config export/import.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

This build is mostly about the things that were missing rather than new switches on top of old ones.

**Config export and import** - everything you have configured (options, per-app rules, custom parameters, whitelist) goes into one JSON file on your storage. Import merges rather than replaces, so keys the backup does not contain are left alone. Useful when moving to a new device or sharing a setup.

**CPU frequency limits** - the profiles used to change the governor and nothing else. They now set scaling_max_freq and scaling_min_freq too, snapped to frequencies your kernel actually advertises. Ranges are 10-45 percent for powersave up to 60-100 for gaming.

**Range checking for custom parameters** - if a node has min and max files next to it, a value outside that range is refused before it is ever written. There is a force option if you know what you are doing.

**LMK and memory pressure** - min_free_kbytes scaled by installed RAM, lowmemorykiller minfree per profile, watermark tuning. This is usually the real reason background apps get killed, and it was not covered before.

**ZRAM sizing** - if zram0 has no size yet it gets 75 percent of RAM, with mkswap and swapon. Existing sizes are left alone.

**Thermal zone selection** - unlocking thermal no longer disables every zone blindly. You choose which ones, cpu and gpu by default. A new zones command lists every zone with its type, mode and temperature.

**Autopilot** - follows the system battery saver and can force a profile during a time window, including windows that cross midnight.

Everything from earlier versions is still there: four profiles, adaptive switching, charge limiting, app standby management, per-app policies, display tuning, boot-failure rollback, wipe protection and the WebUI, now with 8 tabs.

releases.body:
Drop the zip into the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

New in this build:

**CPU frequency limits** - profiles now set scaling_max_freq and scaling_min_freq, not just the governor. The range is picked from the frequencies your kernel actually exposes, so nothing is hardcoded. Toggle with the CPU 频率上下限 switch.

**Boot-failure rollback** - the module counts boots. If the system does not come up three times in a row, it rolls back every kernel and custom parameter it changed, writes the disable flag and turns itself off. This is what protects you when a custom parameter turns out to be wrong.

**Wipe protection** - a new guard with three modes:
- 增强模式: kills the process the moment a wipe command is seen
- 普通模式: pauses and asks you first, through the WebUI
- 不防护: logs only

It watches running processes and boot scripts for rm -rf on system paths, mkfs, dd to block devices, fastboot wipe/erase/format and shred. Temporary paths such as /tmp, /cache and /data/local/tmp are deliberately left alone.

Also: updateJson is now set, so the manager can tell you about new versions.

Everything from before is unchanged: four profiles, adaptive switching, charge limiting, app standby management, per-app policies, custom parameters, display tuning, initrc services and the WebUI.

releases.body:
Drop the zip into the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

**If you had v3.0.2 installed, uninstall it first.** The module id changed from `ksu_tuner` to
`KernelSU-Tuner` to match the registered id, so the manager treats them as two different modules.

What changed in this build:

- `module.prop` and `module.yaml` now use `id=KernelSU-Tuner`, matching the registered id
- module paths follow the id, so the module now lives at `/data/adb/modules/KernelSU-Tuner`
- the initrc file and its service names were renamed to match
- the runtime data directory intentionally stays at `/data/adb/ksu_tuner` so existing configuration survives

Everything else is unchanged from v3.0.2:

- Four profiles (powersave / balanced / performance / gaming) driving CPU governor, GPU levels, IO scheduler and readahead, VM tunables, network stack, DNS and ZRAM compression
- Adaptive switching based on temperature, screen state and charging, with hysteresis
- Charge limiting with automatic resume
- App Standby Bucket management with a per-app whitelist
- Per-app profiles driven by whichever app is in the foreground
- Custom sysfs and proc parameter editor, every change backed up first
- Refresh rate and touch sampling tuning
- initrc services
- WebUI console, no external dependencies

📝 更新日志 ## ⬆️ v2.12.3 → v2.12.5 (2026-10-12) ### 🔧 功能改进 - **移除废弃宏并消除 unsafe 代码** 🦀 - 清理废弃宏并移除 unsafe 代码，提升代码安全性。 ### 🪲 问题修复 - **修复配置解析无法读取整数型浮点** ⚙️ - 修复 `config.toml` 中 `1.0` 这类整数型浮点参数被忽略、不生效的问题。 - **修复 WebUI 保存配置时整数字段被序列化为浮点** 🌐 - 保存后配置文件不再出现 `40.0` 这类写法，与手动编辑的结果保持一致。
📝 CHANGELOG ## ⬆️ v2.12.3 → v2.12.5 (October 12, 2026) ### 🔧 Improvements - **Remove deprecated macros and eliminate unsafe code** 🦀 - Cleaned up deprecated macros and removed unsafe code for better safety. ### 🐛 Bug Fixes - **Fix integer-valued floats being unreadable during config parsing** ⚙️ - Values such as `1.0` in `config.toml` are no longer ignored, so those parameters now take effect. - **Fix integer fields being serialized as floats when saving from the WebUI** 🌐 - Saved configuration no longer contains values like `40.0`, matching the result of editing the file by hand.

## 下载哪个？

- **多数人**：`QSC-Battery_v*-full.zip`（双守护 + WebUI，可内嵌伴侣 APP；在线更新也指向它）
- **只要脚本、包要小**：`…-lite.zip`（无 WebUI / 无内嵌 APK / 无守护）
- **其它模块包**：`-rust` / `-c` 只带对应守护；`-sh` 有 WebUI、守护可后装
- **`QSC-Battery_v*.apk`**：伴侣 APP；非 lite 模块刷入时也可选装，不必单独下
- **`qscd-rust-*` / `qscd-c-*`**：事件守护单文件；一般由 full 自带或 WebUI 下载，**不要当模块刷**

完整说明：[安装与升级](https://eikeitsu.github.io/QSC-Battery/guide/install.html)

## 更新说明

- **KernelSU Next 模块横幅**：增加模块背景横幅，使用ksu next管理器开启模块背景横幅可以给模块增加图片背景；
- **KernelSU 模块仓库**：仓库根目录增加 `module.yaml`（便于提交 modules.kernelsu.org），为将模块提交至ksu官方模块仓库做准备
- **音量键 volkey**：`bin/volkey`（`EVIOCGRAB`）供安装 customize 与 Action 共用，避免 BakaSU 等管理器不吞键时弹出系统音量条；SukiSU 管理器常自吞 KeyEvent。缺二进制时回退 `getevent`
- **Lint**：接入 `lint:py`（ruff）、`lint:clang`、`lint:rust`、`lint:kotlin`（缺工具本机跳过 / CI 强制）；`format:all` 与 lint-staged 覆盖 py / C / Rust / Kotlin

## 下载哪个？

- **多数人**：`QSC-Battery_v*-full.zip`（双守护 + WebUI，可内嵌伴侣 APP；在线更新也指向它）
- **只要脚本、包要小**：`…-lite.zip`（无 WebUI / 无内嵌 APK / 无守护）
- **其它模块包**：`-rust` / `-c` 只带对应守护；`-sh` 有 WebUI、守护可后装
- **`QSC-Battery_v*.apk`**：伴侣 APP；非 lite 模块刷入时也可选装，不必单独下
- **`qscd-rust-*` / `qscd-c-*`**：事件守护单文件；一般由 full 自带或 WebUI 下载，**不要当模块刷**

完整说明：[安装与升级](https://eikeitsu.github.io/QSC-Battery/guide/install.html)

## 更新说明

- **KernelSU Next 模块横幅**：增加模块背景横幅，使用ksu next管理器开启模块背景横幅可以给模块增加图片背景；
- **KernelSU 模块仓库**：仓库根目录增加 `module.yaml`（便于提交 modules.kernelsu.org），为将模块提交至ksu官方模块仓库做准备
- **音量键 volkey**：`bin/volkey`（`EVIOCGRAB`）供安装 customize 与 Action 共用，避免 BakaSU 等管理器不吞键时弹出系统音量条；SukiSU 管理器常自吞 KeyEvent。缺二进制时回退 `getevent`
- **Lint**：接入 `lint:py`（ruff）、`lint:clang`、`lint:rust`、`lint:kotlin`（缺工具本机跳过 / CI 强制）；`format:all` 与 lint-staged 覆盖 py / C / Rust / Kotlin

## AEGIS // FIREWALL v1.0.0

First public release.

- Blacklist and whitelist modes, each with its own rule set
- Per-app control for Wi-Fi, mobile data, VPN, LAN and roaming, IPv4 and IPv6
- Host rules: block or allow a domain, IP or CIDR, optionally per port and protocol, per app or for all apps
- Temporary access (15 min, 1 h, 8 h) that reverts on its own
- Screen-off blocking with a configurable delay
- Rules for every Android user: Dual apps, Second space, work profiles
- Rules applied at boot, before the device is unlocked, in one atomic iptables-restore per address family
- Watchdog that restores the OUTPUT hook if the system removes it
- Live connections per app with one-tap address blocking
- Per-app blocked counters on any kernel, plus kernel LOG when available
- Profiles, backup and restore
- Lockdown kill switch in the WebUI and on the module Action button
- Diagnostics: kernel capability probe, hook state, daemon log, restore errors

Requires a kernel with the iptables owner match (all GKI kernels). The installer checks this and aborts if it is missing.

releases.body:
# Changelog

## 0.1.2-stable - 2026-10-11

### Tricky Store manager
- Complete port of Tricky Addon (Update Target List):
  - Target list with modes, per-app policy, search, bulk selection, DenyList, unnecessary
    apps, system apps and auto-add.
  - Keyboxes from AOSP, "unknown", a local file, the keybox repository and custom providers,
    with import and export.
  - Prop settings, default policy with *Today*, help, keyboard shortcuts and its 23
    translations, including right-to-left languages.
- One manager for Tricky Store (`config.ini` and legacy `target.txt`), TEESimulator
  (`config.json`) and OhMyKeymint (`config.toml` + `injector.toml`).
  - The validation rules follow each module's own sources.
  - Unknown sections, comments and keys are preserved.
- Optional WebUI entry on the keystore module (plus the action button on Magisk), and the
  TSupport-Advance auto-target stop flag.
- Tricky Addon's in-app translation update, translation guide and Telegram link.
- Checked against the real modules on a KernelSU device, which found and fixed:
  - OhMyKeymint v1.2.0 rejected our `injector.toml` (an unknown `version` key) while the
    WebUI reported success. `[scoop.<package>]` tables are now read and written like
    OhMyKeymint's own parser does.
  - The "unknown" keybox now gives each key a two-certificate chain. Tricky Addon's
    single-certificate keybox only loads on Tricky Store: TEESimulator and OhMyKeymint
    refuse it.
  - TEESimulator accepts EC-only keyboxes, such as the RKP workbench exports.
  - Saving tells when OhMyKeymint needs a restart to apply a change.

### WebUI
- Rebuilt on Vue 3.5, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn-vue.
  - A black and white theme, light or dark, where color only marks errors, success and
    warnings.
  - Designed for phones along Material 3 Expressive:
    - 48dp touch targets and a visible response to every press.
    - Round buttons that square up while pressed, segmented lists, and spring motion.
    - A large title that collapses into the 64dp app bar, for one-handed reach.
    - Tonal gray surfaces instead of borders and shadows, with contrast checked
      against WCAG.
  - Menus, tabs and button groups mirror in right-to-left languages too.
  - Follows the KernelSU manager's window insets.
  - The Android back gesture closes dialogs and sheets.
- Every tool in 14 languages: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean,
  Spanish, French, German, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Vietnamese and
  Indonesian.
- Help: long links and code wrap inside the page, and two slips in upstream translations
  (a link missing its parenthesis, a code span closed with a quote) no longer show raw
  Markdown.
- Every tool is a self-contained feature folder, discovered automatically.
  - Features plug into each other only through extension points.
  - Every backend response is validated against a schema.
- A tool whose backend feature is missing or on another contract version is disabled
  instead of misreading data.
- Unit tests (Vitest) and end-to-end tests (Playwright against a mock KernelSU host) with
  light, dark, right-to-left and Chinese screenshots.
- Contract tests run every API call through `duckctl.sh` and a real `duckd` build and
  parse the results with the WebUI's schemas.
- Device tests (`scripts/device-test.sh`) drive the WebUI inside the real KernelSU manager
  with each keystore module installed.
- Loads as seven files instead of about eighty. The KernelSU manager reads each request
  through a root shell, so this halved the load time on a slow device.
- Type-checked on the TypeScript 7 engine through typescript-native-bridge.

### Backend
- `duckd` builds its CLI from a feature registry. `duckd features` reports the compiled-in
  features, and each feature can be built alone.
- New `system` feature: module and device summary, stable and canary updates with changelog,
  output files, command history, uninstall and reboot.
- RKP profiles read their device defaults from AOSP build properties.
- Updated RustCrypto to its current generation (p256/p384 0.14, ed25519/x25519 3, aes-gcm
  0.11, x509-cert 0.3). Keys derived from saved seeds are pinned by regression tests.

### Module
- Scripts follow the KernelSU module guide:
  - Late-load support (`late-load.sh`).
  - A late prop pass after boot for values the system sets late.
  - The module description goes into KernelSU's temporary config.
- Magisk runs the boot-completed work from `service.sh`.
- The prop handler adds `ro.boot.vbmeta.size`, and applies the boot hash even when the
  handler is disabled, as upstream does.
- Uninstalling removes entry links, flags and saved data.

### Tooling
- CI fails when any source file in any language exceeds 600 lines.
- CI: NDK r30, Node 24, pnpm 12, WebUI lint/format/unit/E2E, per-feature builds.
- Canary artifacts are the installable module directory.
- Dependabot opens one pull request per major update.
releases.name: v0.1.2-stable

## 版本 8.5.2（2026-10-11）

### 应用代理

- 代理模式关闭时保留搜索框；切换模式不再清空关键词或退出搜索，重新启用后可继续筛选应用。

releases.body:
2026.08.26

---

- 适配 Android 17 QPR2 Beta 3
- 新增 [HyperOS Runtime 支持](https://github.com/LSPosed/ZygiskNext/blob/main/docs/hyos_runtime.md)
- 修复部分情况下 Zygisk 功能意外失效的问题
- 修复 32 位 ARM 设备上的潜在异常
- 调整 WebView 子进程 umount 方式，交由 Root 方案统一管理

---

- Supports Android 17 QPR2 Beta 3
- Adds [HyperOS Runtime support](https://github.com/LSPosed/ZygiskNext/blob/main/docs/hyos_runtime.md)
- Fixed an issue where Zygisk functionality would unexpectedly fail in some cases
- Fixed potential anomalies on 32-bit ARM devices
- Adjusted the WebView child process umount mechanism, now managed by Root solution.

---
